feat[agents][devenv]: boot a lean template profile against the full package set

[PROBLEM]
The operator recovered the gist's real design intent: it was the
initialized-template .spacemacs, deliberately lean so the devenv never
initializes the full desktop config — availability without startup
bloat. The current design boots the full 60-layer desktop dotfile,
reintroducing the bloat the gist existed to avoid. It also hides a
latent hazard: booting ANY leaner dotfile against the full baked elpa
with spacemacs' default install mode (used-only) UNINSTALLS every
package the lean set doesn't use — deleting at boot what the build
paid to install.

[ROOT-CAUSE]
One dotfile was serving two conflated roles: the build manifest (which
packages the tarball installs — wants the full desktop superset) and
the boot profile (what the devenv initializes — wants the template
minimum). A single file forces all-or-nothing.

[CHANGE]
Split the roles. The desktop dotfile remains the build manifest,
unchanged. Boot copies a committed lean profile
(dotfiles/agents/devenv/spacemacs.el — the gist's role, now versioned):
template-shaped, spacemacs-base, no layers declared, the custom layer
path kept resolvable for on-demand loading, and
dotspacemacs-install-packages 'used-but-keep-unused so the baked elpa
survives lean boots. Consequence documented in both script headers:
desktop-dotfile package additions reach the devenv via tarball
rebuilds, not the boot top-up. The profile was load-tested with the
devenv emacs (both load-bearing values verified); the suite pins the
preservation flag, the layer path, and that boot copies the profile
rather than the desktop dotfile.

subject: fix[emacs][direnv]: remove global direnv-mode that strips git from exec-path
message:
fix[emacs][direnv]: remove global direnv-mode that strips git from exec-path

[PROBLEM]
Magit intermittently died with "process-file: Searching for program: No
such file or directory, git". One magit command worked; the next could
not find git. Git never moved -- Emacs had dropped the directory that
holds it from `exec-path'.

[ROOT-CAUSE]
The config ran two mutually incompatible direnv integrations at once.
The coding layer enables envrc (`envrc-global-mode'), which is
buffer-local: it overrides `exec-path'/`process-environment' only in
buffers under a direnv directory, always derived from the global
defaults, and never touches the global values. The kaizen layer
additionally enabled `direnv-mode' from the global `direnv' package. On
`post-command-hook', direnv-mode runs

    (setq exec-path (append (parse-colon-path PATH) (list exec-directory)))

-- it REPLACES the global `exec-path' with the current directory's
direnv PATH. Visiting a project whose direnv PATH omits git (a `use nix'
devshell usually does) strips git from the global `exec-path', so the
next process-file anywhere -- including magit's next git call -- fails.
Driving the real `direnv-update-directory-environment' against a
git-less PATH reproduces it exactly: git flips from reachable to
unreachable in every buffer. That same global write also corrupts the
pristine global environment envrc treats as its baseline, so the two
cannot coexist.

[CHANGE]
Keep the buffer-local integration; remove the global one. Deleting
`kaizen/init-direnv' and its `direnv' package entry stops direnv-mode
from ever activating, so nothing rewrites the global `exec-path' behind
magit's back and git stays reachable everywhere. envrc still delivers
full direnv support, now only in the buffer where the user works, never
leaking into unrelated buffers. A comment at the envrc init records it
as the sole, deliberately buffer-local direnv integration so the global
variant does not creep back.

Rejected alternatives: dropping envrc and keeping direnv-mode preserves
the global-clobber failure; pinning `magit-git-executable' to an
absolute path hides one symptom while leaving compile, lsp, and shell
exposed to the same global mutation.

subject: fix[emacs][coding]: merge PRs at the head OID forge has on record
message:
fix[emacs][coding]: merge PRs at the head OID forge has on record

[PROBLEM]
forge-merge on any pull request whose head branch was never checked out
locally aborts with "<branch> cannot be dereferenced as a commit" before
issuing the API request. Agent-authored PRs (claude/*) are merged
straight from the forge buffer without a checkout, so every such merge
fails.

[ROOT-CAUSE]
forge-merge derives the API's expectedHeadOid safety token ("merge only
if the head is still X") by resolving the PR's branch NAME against local
git refs: (magit-commit-oid (forge--pullreq-branch-internal pullreq)).
A bare name like claude/... resolves only through refs/heads/*, which
exists solely after a checkout; git does not fall back to origin/<name>.
Magit 4.6.0 obsoleted magit-rev-hash (nil on failure, so the token was
skipped and the merge went through) and forge's migration to
magit-commit-oid dropped the noerror flag, turning the silent nil into a
hard abort. Underneath sits a structural mismatch: the token is a fact
about the PR as last synced -- forge's own record holds it in head-rev
-- and the local branch namespace was never an authoritative source for
it (a stale local branch would send a wrong OID).

[CHANGE]
Override forge-merge (advice installed in coding/post-init-forge) with a
body that feeds forge--merge-pullreq the record's head-rev; a nil
head-rev skips the API-side check exactly as the pre-4.6.0 code did.
Sourcing the token from the record keeps its freshness semantics ("merge
exactly what the buffer shows") and works regardless of local state.
Alternatives rejected: advising magit-commit-oid (globally changes magit
semantics for one caller's benefit) and checking the branch out before
merging (adds local state the workflow deliberately avoids). The new
suite coding/tests/forge-merge-test.el pins the behaviour in a bare
batch Emacs, where any relapse into local-ref interrogation fails as a
void function.

subject: fix[emacs][coding]: stop the post-merge cleanup from fabricating branches
message:
fix[emacs][coding]: stop the post-merge cleanup from fabricating branches

[PROBLEM]
Merging a pull request from the forge buffer succeeds but still ends on
an error:

  git branch claude/token-metadata-refactor-4appkw tmrtx/claude/...
  git branch claude/token-metadata-refactor-4appkw --set-upstream-to=main
  git checkout main
  git pull --ff-only tmrtx
  git branch -d claude/token-metadata-refactor-4appkw
  error: the branch '...' is not fully merged

A stray local branch is left behind, and the buffer never refreshes, so
the merged PR still reads as open.

[ROOT-CAUSE]
The previous commit fixed the merge itself; this is the cleanup that
runs after it, and it fails the same never-checked-out PR twice more.

forge--merge-pullreq reaches the branch to clean up through
(or (forge--pullreq-branch-active pullreq) (forge--branch-pullreq
pullreq)). A PR that was never checked out has no active branch, so the
fallback CREATES one -- the first two git calls above -- purely so the
next line can delete it.

That deletion then uses "git branch -d", whose "is it fully merged?"
test git answers from local ancestry. A rebase or squash merge rewrites
the commits, so git says no and the command errors out. The question was
already answered authoritatively by the forge, which merged the PR at a
known OID; git is being asked to re-derive a fact it cannot see.

Both failures share one root: the cleanup treats local git state as the
authority on a pull request whose truth lives in the forge.

[CHANGE]
Replace the cleanup with coding/forge-merge--cleanup, which acts only on
a branch that already exists -- never fabricating one -- and deletes it
with "-D" when it is exactly the commit the forge merged. When it is not
(local commits never pushed, so they exist nowhere else) the branch is
kept and the user told: that is the case git's protection is actually
for, which is why the fix compares rather than always forcing. The
refresh now sits outside every branch, because forge--pull skips its own
refresh whenever a callback is supplied.

The cleanup is a lambda buried inside the github forge--merge-pullreq
method, so correcting it means redefining that method; only the callback
body differs, and the mutation mirrors upstream verbatim.

Three cases pin the behaviour in coding/tests/forge-merge-test.el, where
forge--branch-pullreq signals if called so fabrication fails the suite
outright. A scratch smoke run additionally exercised the cleanup against
a real rebase-merged git repository with magit loaded, confirming both
that "git branch -d" fails there and that the branch is pruned without
error afterwards.

fix[emacs][coding]: expand forge's merge macro at load time, not compile time

[PROBLEM]
The previous two commits had no effect in a real session. Merging a pull
request still ended on:

  Git error: Your local changes to the following files would be
             overwritten by merge
  Git error: the branch 'claude/cognition-help-command-w7sfx6' is not
             fully merged

The second line is the tell: "not fully merged" can only come from
"git branch -d", and the replacement cleanup never runs -d. Forge's own
cleanup was still in place.

The method redefinition that installs the replacement cleanup calls
forge-mutate, one of forge's MACROS. This layer enables compile-angel,
which byte-compiles packages.el on load, in sessions where forge has not
been loaded yet. The compiler therefore cannot know the symbol is a
macro; it compiles a CALL to a function of that name, which dies at
runtime with void-function forge-mutate and takes the rest of the
:config block with it.

The advice-add sits before that form in the same block, which is why the
merge itself worked while the cleanup stayed forge's own -- a split that
made the fix look installed while half of it never ran.

A separate defect surfaced in the same report: the cleanup moves the
working tree without checking it is free to move, so "git checkout"
aborts whenever anything is uncommitted, which is most of the time.

Quote the method definition and eval it, so expansion happens when the
:config block runs -- where forge is loaded by definition -- instead of
when the compiler sees the file. The form is otherwise unchanged and
still mirrors forge-github.el verbatim.

An unclean working tree now skips the local tidy-up entirely, deletion
included, since the branch may be the one checked out; nothing about
tidying up after a merge justifies disturbing work in progress. The
merge still lands and still shows up in the buffer.

The compiled artifact is where this bug lived, so the unit suite cannot
see it. A scratch smoke run byte-compiles the real coding/post-init-forge

fix[dotfiles][emacs/roam]: leave point in the new note's body, not its headline

[PROBLEM]
Every note created with the `nn' snippet came out with a garbage word
welded onto its heading: a note typed as "hierarchy of controls" was
written as "hierarchy of controls-eliminate".  The ID and CAPTURE_TIME
properties were correct, so only the heading needed fixing by hand --
every single time.

[ROOT-CAUSE]
`roam/-create-new-node' left point at the end of the heading it had just
written.  A heading is ordinary buffer text, so the title's last word was
then the symbol before point -- and every completion and expansion
mechanism in this configuration extends the symbol before point: corfu's
auto-popup over `cape-dabbrev' (coding layer), `hippie-expand' and
abbrev expansion (technical-writing layer).  Whatever they offered for
"controls" was appended inside the heading.

The title itself was never at risk: it is read through `read-string',
whose minibuffer corfu declines to enter, which is why the ID derived
from that same string stayed correct while the heading did not.

A `"\n"' after the title used to keep point off the end of the word.  It
was dropped when the title started being written with `org-edit-headline',
leaving behind only the comment that described it -- so the code carried
the diagnosis but not the guard.

[CHANGE]
Move point to the new entry's body once the heading, ID and capture time
are written, opening a line for it when the entry is followed by a
sibling heading.  This is where the note's text goes anyway, so the
cursor now lands where the user is about to type, and the heading sits
out of reach of anything that completes at point.

Restoring the `"\n"' would have suppressed this one symptom while leaving
point somewhere no completion may fire from by accident rather than by
design; the body is a position that is correct for a reason a reader can
check.

The suite specifies the outcome rather than the cursor's coordinates: it
fires a real `dabbrev' expansion after creating a note and asserts the
heading is unchanged, and asserts that typed text becomes the note's body
while the following sibling stays intact.

feat[dotfiles][emacs/agenda]: resolve LOGBOOK span conflicts around an authoritative span

[PROBLEM]
A retroactive journal entry states when something really happened, but
the entry that was clocked at the time still claims those minutes.
Reconciling the records takes three hand edits per conflict -- reshape
the other entry's span, recompute its duration, repeat in every entry
it overlaps -- and nothing at all helps move a misfiled span through
time.

[ROOT-CAUSE]
org-mode has no notion of one clock span being authoritative over
others: its resolution tooling (org-resolve-clocks) handles idle and
dangling clocks only, so every overlap created on purpose -- retro
filing, span moves -- ends in hand editing.

[CHANGE]
New agenda-layer local package `clock-conflicts` reifies the rule "the
span the user just asserted wins": spans in the current file plus
org-agenda-files that overlap it are trimmed, split, or removed exactly
like the hand fix, running clocks included (the open line moves and
org's in-memory clock follows via org-clock-update-time-maybe).  Two
commands expose it on the flow hydra: agenda/org-clock-resolve-conflicts
makes the entry at point authoritative; agenda/org-clock-move-span
shifts a span back by a duration, forward with "+", or to an "@" start,
then fixes what the move hits.  Files nobody visits are pre-scanned in
a temp buffer and only opened (saved, closed) on a hit, so the
no-conflict case costs one regexp pass per file; buffers mid-edit are
fixed but never saved.  The ERT suite drives the public commands on
real org buffers and pins every yield shape, written before the
implementation.  Alternative considered: advising org-clock-in/out --
rejected because it cannot see hand-written logbooks and couples to org
internals.
